text.p: Eritrean officials suspect the killers of five Belgian tourists and their local driver last month were terrorists, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
"So far, we have no hint as to what kind of people did it, but our number one suspicion is that it was an act of terrorism", Tewolde Woldemichael, head of the ministry's European desk, told Reuters.
The Belgians and the Eritrean driver were ambushed and killed at Filfil, 40-km (25-miles) north of the capital Asmara, on December 27.
A Belgian foreign ministry spokesman said on December 30 the culprits were thought to be bandits.
At first that was also the Eritrean view because the killers stole everything from the car, including identity papers.
But Tewolde said terrorists were now suspected.
He said officials had "some facts about their (the internal opposition's) composition and movements". He would not elaborate.
He accused neighbouring Sudan's National Islamic Front (NIF) government of sponsoring terrorism in Eritrea, saying:
"The NIF is continuously recruiting and sending subversive elements across the border. That is why our suspicion of terrorism is strong," Tewolde said.
Eritrea is the base for Sudan's armed opposition.

Internal opposition to the Eritrean government comes mainly from the ELF-RC (Eritrean Liberation Front-Revolutionary Council), a splinter from the original ELF which parted with the then emerging Eritrean People's Liberation Front (EPLF) in the early days of the war for independence from Ethiopia.

The foreign ministry says the Belgian tourists, four women and a man, were driving from Shibah towards Filfil on the afternoon of Friday, December 27. At high speed they overtook two cars carrying British tourists.
Filfil, with its green valley and forest in otherwise dry and arid Eritrea, is a popular spot for tourists.
The British were halted by Eritrean military and persuaded to spend the night at the military camp at Shibah. Soldiers told them "there are bad people around here".

On the morning of December 28, the British continued their trip toward Filfil, and at 9 A.M. found the ambushed Toyota Land Cruiser. All six victims had been shot dead and the bodies were inside and outside the car.
One Asmara-based diplomat used the word "execution" to describe the killings.
